Hi Mina / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our latest redlines to the Order Form and the short summary (see attached). Our legal team flagged three items that need tightening before procurement can move to signature:

1) Output ownership: we need explicit confirmation that Novum retains ownership of customer inputs and model outputs for our internal use and productization.
2) Training/data use: Novum cannot agree to any clause that allows Redwood to use customer-provided prompts/outputs to further train models without opt-in. We are open to limited, anonymized telemetry for safety.
3) Feedback license: any license to use feedback should be narrowly scoped to security/bug fixes, and not for commercial model training.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and propose language that preserves our rights while allowing Redwood to operate (e.g., aggregated safety telemetry, removal of PII)? Procurement is on a tight timeline — we need a response by end of day Wednesday.

Thanks Mina — I reviewed Novum's redlines and drafted targeted language below. High-level legal position: we can and should preserve Novum's ownership of their inputs and outputs (subject to the service license), while carving a narrow operational license to Redwood limited to delivering the service. We must also preserve limited telemetry use for safety and product stability; however, we can agree to an explicit prohibition on using customer prompts/outputs to train our general models unless the customer provides opt-in.

Suggested redline snippets (to drop into Order Form / MSA):

1) Ownership of Inputs and Outputs
"Company retains all right, title and interest in and to Customer Data and Customer Outputs. Redwood hereby grants Customer a perpetual, royalty-free license to use Customer Outputs for its internal business purposes and productization."

2) Service Operational License (to enable service delivery)
"Customer hereby grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use Customer Data and Customer Outputs solely to perform the Services, provide support, debug issues, and operate and improve the performance and reliability of the Services (the 'Operational License'). Such Operational License does not include the right to incorporate Customer Data or Customer Outputs into Redwood model weights or to create a standalone dataset for the purpose of training general-purpose models."

3) Telemetry & Aggregated Safety Data
"Redwood may collect aggregated and de-identified telemetry necessary for monitoring, security, and service improvements. Such telemetry shall not include Customer PII or verbatim Customer Outputs and shall not be used to retrain Redwood's general models unless Customer provides prior written opt-in."

4) Feedback License
"Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use feedback or issue reports provided by Customer solely for debugging, security patches, and operational improvements. The Feedback License expressly excludes the right to use such feedback for commercial model training or resale."

I've taken care to keep the operational license as narrow as possible while enabling us to fix issues and maintain an SLA. If Novum insists on additional audit or delete-rights for telemetry that's reasonable; we can add a contractual right to periodic telemetry reports and an obligation to delete customer-specific logs on request.

I'll attach a redlined Order Form with the snippets incorporated and a one-page memo for the sales/procurement team.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the thoughtful draft. A few items from our side:

- Ownership: the ownership clause looks fine, but we need to add an express representation that Redwood will not assert rights in Customer Outputs against Novum's customers.
- Telemetry: we appreciate the de-identification carveout. For compliance we need a contractual right to quarterly telemetry reports and the ability to request deletion of logs relating to a specific incident or dataset (with a reasonable fee to cover costs).
- Feedback license: the exclusion for commercial training is good. We need to clarify "feedback" to exclude product feature requests or ideas that might be used in future models.

Procurement timeline: if we can resolve wording on the above three points today, our procurement director Tom Li can sign and route for final approval tomorrow. Otherwise we risk a week delay.
